title: State relabelling commutes with one step
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $e$ be a bijection from its state set to another state set, let $x$ be an input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. Taking one step of the relabelled machine from the configuration obtained by applying $e$ to the state of $c$ gives the same configuration as taking one step of $M$ from $c$ and then applying $e$ to its state.
hypotheses_covered: A multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes
A bijection between its state set and another state set
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$,
let $e$ be a bijection from $S$ to another state set, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on a fixed input word.  Then one step of the machine
obtained by relabelling the states of $M$ along $e$, taken from the
configuration $c$ with state renamed along $e$, equals the configuration
obtained by one step of $M$ from $c$ with state renamed along $e$.  The
equality includes the case of a halted $c$, where both sides leave the
configuration unchanged.
